paragraphs.source_en: Once the repairs to Okazaki Castle were complete, Tokugawa Ieyasu moved swiftly. After briefly withdrawing from Yoshida Castle to Hamamatsu, he immediately crossed the Ōi River and invaded Suruga. He first kindled the flames of war at Okabe, ordering crops harvested while skirmishing outside Kunō Castle, then advanced his troops to the outskirts of Sunpu Castle. All this was intended to ascertain whether Shingen was alive or dead before deciding his next move.

paragraphs.source_en: In the summer of the first year of Tenshō, Nobuyasu of Okazaki obeyed his father Ieyasu's command and set out from Okazaki Castle, advancing north through the Asuke and Busetsu regions to break open another route from Shinano into Okazaki.
